notes: The Space panel now tracks missiles, torpedoes and rockets coming at you. Each one is drawn on the scope (and in the cockpit view) where it is, with its seconds to impact, and the line at the scope's bottom left says what lands first.

Chaff help: the Chaff button turns red when something lands within 15 seconds and your chaff won't still be up then, and is lit while chaff is up. One release lasts about 19 seconds and blows up whatever arrives meanwhile.
The Simulator drill now releases chaff by itself at that moment. If a release doesn't come out (none left) it stops trying until the next run.

Auto radar now sends 'radar projectiles' (the same ships and planets, plus every projectile), every 3 seconds while something is coming at you and right after a launch, still kept off the main screen. The Simulator drill uses these quiet radars too.
Fixed: lines the game counts, like 'Incoming rocket from ... [x2]' and 'The ship is hit by a rocket! [x2]', count as two.
history: The Space panel now tracks missiles, torpedoes and rockets coming at you. Each one is drawn on the scope (and in the cockpit view) where it is, with its seconds to impact, and the line at the scope's bottom left says what lands first.

Chaff help: the Chaff button turns red when something lands within 15 seconds and your chaff won't still be up then, and is lit while chaff is up. One release lasts about 19 seconds and blows up whatever arrives meanwhile.
The Simulator drill now releases chaff by itself at that moment. If a release doesn't come out (none left) it stops trying until the next run.

Auto radar now sends 'radar projectiles' (the same ships and planets, plus every projectile), every 3 seconds while something is coming at you and right after a launch, still kept off the main screen. The Simulator drill uses these quiet radars too.
Fixed: lines the game counts, like 'Incoming rocket from ... [x2]' and 'The ship is hit by a rocket! [x2]', count as two.

The Space panel's weapons are bars now: each one fills while it recharges and says how long it has left, then turns green when the game says it's charged. The time is learned from your own fights, per weapon.

New: a Scan button on the Target card. It sends stat for your target and shows its shields and hull as bars, with how long ago you scanned it. When the game says its shields failed, its shield bar drops to 0. Its energy, speed and whom it targets are in the name's tooltip.

The Target card counts what your target fires at you. A scan that lists its missiles, torpedoes and rockets shows how many it has left; a ship you haven't scanned is taken as fully loaded for its kind (once you've scanned or looked at one), less what it fired.
The MISSILE INCOMING warning counts the missiles on their way and stays until the last one hits or blows up in your chaff (missiles take 11 to 16 seconds to land). Before, the first hit ended it.
Fixed: flight mode ends by itself when you leave the ship, so the map and chat go back to half and half when a simulator run ends.

New: flight mode. The Flight button on the Space tab (or 'space flight on') gives the tab about 70% of the right side; the chat stays below it, smaller, with all its tabs. Click it again to go back. It's off at every start.

New in flight mode: the cockpit view, the fight as seen out of the front of your ship. Ships ahead are drawn by their kind and get bigger as they come closer, your target sits in a bracket (amber while tracking, red once locked), and a ship beside or behind you is an arrow at the edge showing which way to turn. The stars swing past as the ship turns to a new course.
The view shows what happens: bolts when you fire, a red flash when you're hit, an explosion where a ship is destroyed, and a blinking MISSILE INCOMING while one is on its way.
Click to fly: click a ship in the view to turn to it and target it, or click empty space to set course that way.

The Space tab has a radar scope now, like the System tab's: you in the middle and every ship, planet and star of your last radar around you. A ship that targets you is red, your target has a ring, a small arrow says above or below you, and a white line shows the way you're flying (dashed while the ship is still turning). Click a ship on it to turn to it and target it; the two buttons in its corner zoom.

New: Auto radar, the chip at the scope's corner (or 'space radar on'). While the Space panel is showing it sends a radar every 6 seconds and keeps the answer off the main screen, so the scope stays current without the flood. A radar you type or click yourself shows as it always did. It never goes out while you're locking on.

The Space panel's buttons can't break your lock any more. Target turns to the ship first and then targets it, and anything you click during the 3 seconds of tracking waits and is sent the moment the lock is there. Chaff is the exception: it always goes at once.
The Simulator drill knows two more of the game's answers: nothing ready to fire, and a ship that's already gone.

New: a Space tab beside Map / System / Galaxy, for space fights. In a cockpit it shows bars for your shields, hull and energy, the ships around you (click one to target it), your target and its lock, a light per weapon (green = ready, amber = charging) and buttons for Target, Face, Fire, Recharge, Chaff and Radar. Pop out turns it into a window you can move and size, and the chat stays where it is. Type 'space' to open it.
The Space tab shows from the next start of Mudlet after this update; until then 'space' opens the window.

New drill on Automation > Training: Simulator, for the space combat skills. Stand in a holosimulator pod whose instructions say 'join fighter', pick Simulator and press Start (or type 'training sim'). It joins and starts the fighter scenario, and for each drone turns to it, targets it, waits for the lock and fires whenever a gun is charged, recharging the shields between drones. When the ship is destroyed it joins again, until you press Stop.
Space combat isn't on the bot list, so the Simulator drill only runs at the screen, with bot mode off. It never sends a fight command outside the simulator, and it pauses on anything it doesn't know.

New: the Datapad keeps track of what changes on the datanet. When a crawl with 'Read saved pages again' on, or 'read again' on a page, finds a page different from your copy, your old copy is kept and the change goes on the new Changes page (the Changes button, top right, or 'dpad changes'): when it was seen, which page, and how many lines were added, removed and edited.

Click a change to see it: added lines in green with a +, removed lines in red with a -, and an edited line shown once with its old words struck out and the new ones after them. Older and Newer step through a page's earlier changes, and a page that has changed says so at its top.

The Datapad's Crawl button now opens a Crawl page with a control for everything: a check box per clan, switches for reading saved pages again (to pick up changes) and for members-only pages, and Start, Stop, Resume and Start over buttons with a progress bar. Before, it could only start the plain crawl.

New: a Crawl button on the Datapad (top right). It reads from the game every page your saved pages link to that you don't have yet. It says Stop crawl while it runs and Resume crawl after a stop, and the Datapad's bottom line shows how far it is. It replaces the 'Fetch from the game' links on the home page.
A crawl now also follows the links of pages you read yourself, not only what each clan's home page leads to.
The Datapad keeps every datanet page you read in the game. Type 'datanet MS:/public/home' or click a datanet link: the page is saved and opens in the Datapad. Before, only a crawl saved pages.
In the Datapad, a link to a page that isn't saved yet reads it from the game, and every page has a 'read again' link for a fresh copy. Both use datapad charge, like reading it yourself.
The old DataNet package isn't needed any more: if you still have it, it's switched off. Its 'showdata' and 'hidedata' now open and close the Datapad.
Fixed: the crawler saved the game's 'Access Denied' as if it were a page.

Auto Cargo no longer runs you past the 2,000,000 credits you can carry (past that the game drops the rest on the floor). Each stop it reads your gold and looks a whole loop ahead. If you'd go over, it walks to the nearest bank it knows a way to, deposits into the accounts with the most room, walks back and carries on, leaving enough to keep buying.

A pad with no mapped way to a bank (a locked door, a lift) leaves it to a later stop. If this very sale would go over, it pauses before selling and tells you. Settings are on the Auto Cargo page's Credits card, or 'autocargo bank on|off' and 'autocargo keep <credits>|auto'.
A room where a deposit or withdrawal works now counts as a bank, even if its title doesn't say [Bank].

Auto Cargo stops by itself and stays stopped until you click Start: right there when someone else says your name or sends you a tell, and at the next planet after 2 hours since you last clicked Start or Resume. Both are on the page's Stops by itself card, or 'autocargo name on|off' and 'autocargo hours <n>|off'.

Logs are easier to read and smaller: the same line several times in a row is written once with a count (x12 in the Journal), prompts are saved plain, and Everything else starts a new file each month. Older months are links on its page, and a search offers them at its end.
New: Character > Voice, a page for your accent: on or off, style, strength, your word swaps and a box to try a line. A bare 'accent' opens it.
New: links on the Datapad's home page to fetch pages from the game (all clans, stop, resume), so there's no need to type dncrawl.
One line when the profile loads: the OmiLOTJ version, not a 'Loaded' line from every script.
Fixed: the datanet crawler works with any prompt (with another prompt it lost every page as missing), keeps a page it has read when chat runs on, and says so when it can't save one.
Fixed: a chat line mentioning 'not encrypted' can't move the decrypt drill on.

Less work in the background: the GMCP field list only runs if you turn it on ('gmcp fields on' or 'gmcp watch new'), the corner timers only redraw what changed and stop rising over open windows, and the Ship DB, trade scans and lockers write their files less often.
Old downloaded packages and old Galaxy pictures now clean themselves up.

New: Automation > Crafting, one place for building ships, making, enhancing and stitching armor, repairing gear and craft loops, with a tab and a list for each. Every old typed command still works (autobuildship, aadd, eadd, naaddm, autorepair, craft, mclothing...). It replaces Autobuildship, the LotJ Armor package, Autorepair and the old crafting scripts: the armor loops never really ran, and building could go round for ever with nothing on the floor. Lists are saved now. Not tried in the game yet: tell me what the game says if a job pauses.

While you're botting, building ships never takes or drops parts: those commands aren't on the game's bot list (help botting), and Autobuildship sent them. It works from what you carry and pauses when you run out.
Repairs now put your gear back on with wear (hold only works for held things like a datapad).

New: a study queue on Automation > Training, in place of AutoStudy. studyadd, studystart and the rest still work, the list is saved, and nothing happens unless the queue is running: no more error on every study or a blind 'afk' at the end of a bot cooldown.

New: Character > Combat, in place of CombatStats: accuracy, damage per hit, best hit, dodge rate. Its numbers are right now (it counted misses as hits and never counted 'You miss'), and speech with 'hits you' in it doesn't count.
New: Ships > Places: your speedwalk bookmarks (click to walk), this room's smart exits, taxis on or off, this room's symbol and colour on the map. 'sp' works as before.
Autoflight is gone: nothing could start it, and Fly To took over its job.
If you still have any of those old packages, their triggers and aliases are switched off so nothing answers twice. You can remove them.
Fixed: a semicolon in the Writer or in a hail reply stays in the line. Before, the line was cut in two there, and in a hail the second half went to the game as a command.
Fixed: Auto Cargo only tries another pad when the game really refuses one. Chat or a room's text with words like 'restricted' or 'too large' during a landing used to make it switch pads.
Fixed: when Auto Cargo finishes (Done, or Sell and stop) the page says idle, not Paused, and Resume can't send the last sale again.
Fixed: the docking panel only looks at lines about docking. A ship record's 'Dock:' row or a dockworkers line could mark you docked, and room text about docking clamps could pop the panel up.
Faster: the Journal's 'Everything else' page opens at once, its search takes less than half the time, and the People page has no wait. Search and that page no longer load the whole log into memory.
A damaged save file is now kept aside as <name>.broken-<date> and you're told, in every system. Twelve of them used to treat it as empty and overwrite it on the next save.
Fixed: 'rcc <colour>' colours a room's map symbol again (it errored), 'rcc off' puts it back, and 'rs <letter>' shows on the map right away.
Removed some old one-offs: the Dismantle Ship trigger, gmcpcheck (use 'gmcp') and kkk. Menus also stopped writing a debug file on every click.

Fixed: with 'Start again after the cooldown' on, Training didn't pick up again when the game's 30-minute bot cooldown ended. It now pauses the moment the game says your bot time is up (before, it could send one more command into the AFK and lose track of the cooldown), and carries on when the game says you may bot again.

Fixed: Dossiers re-read the whole clan comms log every time Mudlet started, so people's rank history filled up with the same old ranks over and over, and voices you had named came back as unnamed. It's read once now, as intended.

New training drill: Turbolift security (Automation > Training, or 'training lift'). Stand in a city turbolift and it sends 'secure turbolift', then 'slice turbolift', over and over (about 90 s a try). If the lift is already secure it slices first. Secure and slice are on the bot list, so bot mode works. A ship's own lift can't be secured: the drill pauses and shows the game's line.

New training drill: Ship security (Automation > Training, or 'training ship'). In your ship's cockpit it sends 'secure ship', then 'slice ship', over and over (about 90 s a try). When the ship's own security beats yours it slices first, a failed slice tries again, and a try cut off by a command starts again. Secure and slice are on the bot list, so bot mode works. The corner timer has a Slicing bar now too.

Bot time left is read from what the game sends every second while you bot, so it's right after 'Botting resumed.' too (that line doesn't say how much is left). With 'Start again after the cooldown' on, a resumed bot session now also picks up again after its cooldown.
Behind the scenes: Omi Flight is now three scripts in Ships (Omi Flight, Omi Get Clear, Omi Ship Stats) so each stays a size that's easy to work on. Nothing changes in how anything works.

Your ship's own numbers from the game: sitting in a cockpit, the game sends the ship's top speed, fuel tank, hull and shields, and Flight uses them (Clear to jump timer, fuel range ring, Fly To and Auto Cargo routes) instead of an old 'info' or the stock numbers for its type. The fuel aboard is now read every couple of seconds instead of estimated, and each ship learns its own fuel per parsec from its jumps.

Ships launching or arriving right behind you: they count toward 'clear to jump' the moment the game announces them, a radar is sent to see where they're heading, and if you'd just been told you're clear, the Clear to jump bar comes back until you really are. Moving ships are tracked between radars, so the bar knows when one is flying along with you.

Cash without typing score: the Bank keeps your cash on hand up to date from what the game sends after score, gold and bank moves, and in between from sales (minus their tax), cargo buys, refuels, taxis, shop buys, wages, loot and gifts.

GMCP field list: everything the game sends behind the scenes is now listed for the long run, each field once, with when it first showed up and how often it changes. 'gmcp watch new' prints only fields never seen before (it stays on across restarts, so you can leave it on while you train, fight and fly), 'gmcp fields' writes the list to omi_gmcp_fields.txt. Both are links under 'gmcp'.

Fixed: Ships > Landing Pads and Ship Stats no longer run past the bottom of the window. Landing Pads fills the window with planet cards and puts the rest on more pages (arrows at the top right). Ship Stats' ship list shows as many rows as fit above What if and Cargo run and pages the rest (it opens on the page of the ship you picked), and its stats table pages above the notes under it.

Recording now also keeps everything the game sends behind the scenes (GMCP: your ship's position about every second, its speed and energy, your vitals, the room and more) in its own file, omi_logs\\gmcp\\, named like that session's log. Each line has the time to the millisecond; a kind of message is written in full the first time, then only what changed. It follows rec: nothing from the login screen, and 'rec off' stops both.

New: Character > Gear & goals > All gear: every item in Merr-Sonn's gear directory (102), slot by slot on the left, each slot's items on the right with their benefits and where to get them: the cheapest NPC vendor seen in your shop lists. Player shops buy from NPC vendors and resell for far more, so a shop asking 4x the cheapest price seen is guessed a player shop (Player?); click a shop's kind to set it yourself. Items no shop has shown yet say where to start looking, and 'Your note' keeps what you find. Typed: gear, gear all [slot], gear note <item> = <where>, gear shop <shop> = npc | player | guess.

New: GMCP probe, to see everything the game sends behind the scenes (room, character, ship and more). 'gmcp' lists each kind of message with how often it comes and how many fields it holds (click one to see them all), 'gmcp all' shows every field, 'gmcp watch' prints each change as it arrives (again to stop; 'gmcp watch Char.Vitals' for just one), 'gmcp save' writes it all to omi_gmcp_probe.txt.
'util flyto', 'util lanes' (or 'util galaxy') and 'util train' open those pages too, and 'util help' lists every page.
Fixed: an open Trade window shows new prices after a scan by itself (it used to need the toolbar to know it was open).

Journal: talks with other clans have their own list, People > Journal > Clan comms > External Transmissions. Each '[Incoming Transmission from ...]' or '[Outgoing Transmission to ...]' shows with its message on one line, with how many went in and out and with which clans. Clan comms keeps your own clan's talk. Your whole backlog is sorted in already, and new ones land there by themselves. Faces and People no longer list 'Incoming Transmission from ...' as if it were a person.

Ship DB: owners' names no longer have '[d]' stuck after them. Someone you have a dossier on gets a small file icon in the lists (pink name on the text pages), and a ship's page has an 'open dossier' link next to its owner.

TLC Science Study can be botted: it's the study skill. With bot mode on (Automation > Training) it sends 'bot start' first, pauses when the 2-hour bot time is up, carries on after the cooldown when 'Start again after the cooldown' is on, and sends 'bot stop' when the round is done or stopped.

TLC Science Study keeps going when you stop a study yourself: talking on a channel, a wrong direction or anything else that brings 'You stop studying.' makes it study again a moment later (it used to just wait). Walk out of the hall and it pauses instead; Resume carries on from where you stand.

Fixed: the corner timer's study bar said a study takes 1 s and never learned the real length (about 45 s). The gain line that comes just after a study ends had been timing the next study at half a second. Those times are thrown out and it learns again.

New training drill: TLC Science Study (Automation > Training, or 'tlcstudy'). Stand in the camera hall of the Tarintha Learning Center on Ithor (the Lobby, then west) and Start: it sends 'pra science', then in each of the 18 study halls studies the item until you're an adept of its science (100%), walks to the next hall and finishes in the [Library].

A hall is only skipped when its science is known and already at 100%, or when you press Skip hall (next to Pause / Resume; typed: tlcstudy skip). Study is luck, so it never gives up on its own. Each hall's science is learned the first time the TLC says 'insight into your <science> studies' there (the camera = advanced electronics and the chemistry set = chemistry are known already).

The page lists every hall with its science (or 'not seen yet'), where you are in it, and what this run did there. If it can't find a hall's item it asks: 'tlcstudy item <word>' in that hall, and it remembers the word. 'You are not ready to learn this skill' pauses it (Skip or Resume).

It walks from room to room, and walking isn't on the game's bot list, so it only runs at the screen (not in bot mode). It empties AutoStudy's list at the start so the two don't fight over the study command.
The corner timer's study bar now also ends on 'After some time studying you feel you know more.'

Ship DB keeps every ship's full history: nothing is dropped any more (only the last 20 places were kept). Seeing a ship again with nothing changed counts on the same entry (when you first and last saw it there, how many times, how: in the room, from the cockpit, radar); any change starts a new entry: another place, taking off (launching), another hull under that name, or back after it had left. Back on a pad without it, its entry says 'gone by' and when.

Every ship has a 'full history' page (link on its file and in Dossiers, or 'shipdb history <ship>'): every entry and every locateship answer, newest first, changes and owner changes marked; a rename you confirmed brings the old name's entries along. All of it is also in omi_ships\\history.tsv, ready for Excel.

Once, shortly after loading, your recordings (omi_logs) are read back to the first one: the places ships were seen before the Ship DB kept them all, radar sightings to the second, and old locateship answers (the same answer twice counts once; owners are worked out again from all of them). It works in the background and says what it found.

In space near one planet, the cockpit view and radar count as one place (they made two before), and a cockpit view never marks a ship gone (it leaves out the ship you're in). A pad whose name ends in a space (Alpha Pad at Kala'uun) is now found from the cockpit too.

Writer: all 256 of the game's colours. '256 colours' (next to the colour swatches) opens a picker with the 16 basic colours, the full colour cube and the 24 greys; hover a square for its code, the game's name and hex code (as in 'view256'), click it and Ctrl+V puts it in your text. The colour you picked last is outlined.
Writer: 'Any colour #' takes a hex code (like 1EE896) and copies the game's code for it (&#1EE896, or the short &### code when it's one of the 256). Typed: writer palette.

New: Writer (Character menu, or 'writer'). Write your description and history like in a word processor: type or paste in a big box, and see beside it exactly how the game will show it, in its colours and at its 80 columns, with lines and characters counted against the game's limits.

Writer helpers: colour swatches (click, then Ctrl+V), Paste from Mudlet (right-click > Copy as HTML keeps the colours), Copy / Copy plain, Fit 80, Reflow, Undo, Notepad (edit in your computer's own editor), and the history templates from HELP BIOTEMPLATE.
Load from game reads your current description or history into the box (nothing changes in the game); Save to game types it all into the game's buffer and saves it.
Writer > Colours: paste Mudlet's Copy as HTML (or text with codes) and get the game's colour codes or plain text, ready to copy.

While any writing buffer is open in the game (a note, a bug report, your description), commands from scripts wait until it closes, so Fly To, the Ship DB and the rest can't type into your text any more. Lines you type yourself go in as usual.

Trade routes show what to carry: under every route a small line lists each leg's cargo, where it's bought and sold and for how much, and the gain a unit ("Water  Naboo 6.00 -> Ryloth 17.00  +11.00"). A leg riding a TradeCast is gold with the signal icon.
More routes than fit? Page arrows in each card's title ("< 1 / 23 >") show the next ones; the page stays put when prices update, and a new sort starts at the best again.

Training: a Disguise drill. It applies the disguise slot you pick (74 s, one canister of home repair putty a try), takes it off after a success and goes again; after a failure it simply tries again. It looks first whether you're already wearing one.

Pick the slot on Automation > Training: 'Read slots' fills in your disguises (name, race, saved) and how many you can have; the page also shows about how much putty you have left. Typed: training disguise <slot>, training slot <n>, training slots.
Disguise isn't on the game's bot list, so this drill only runs at the screen (it won't start in bot mode). The corner timer shows a bar for each try.

Trade: prices under 10 credits are read now. The game writes them as "( Price per unit: 6.71 )" with a space, and those were skipped, so the cheapest goods were missing, like water on Mon Cala (6.71) and Naboo (6.00) during today's Coruscant water TradeCast. Scan again (trade scan) to pick them up.
Accent: paths and file names (MS:/public/gear/over, notes.txt, some_name) go out exactly as typed. Before, a word inside a datanet path could be changed.
Accent: a voice can have words that only change when they stand on their own, as an answer ("No." or "No, ..." but not "no training"). 'accent list' shows them.
Accent: a word swapped for one that starts with an apostrophe keeps its capital at the start of a sentence ('Preciate it! 'Bout time.).

Ship upgrade limits: type 'upgradeship <ship> limits' in a garage once and the ranges are kept by themselves (how low and how high every stat, weapon and cargo pod can go on that hull). Ships > Ship Stats now shows each stat's range, a '+N' never goes past the max ('at its max' / 'only +3 to the max'), how many more fit, and what maxing the whole ship would cost in quota and credits. A 'Read limits' button asks the game for you.

Ranges are learned per ship type too, so a ship you haven't read yet shows its type's ranges. Known from the start: YT-1000, JumpMaster 5000, Star Galleon and the AEG-77 Vigo; new types you read are shared with friends in the next update. Any limits you looked at before this update are found in your recordings by themselves.
Cargo pods: every pod holds 500 units (9 pods = 4,500). Ship Stats shows a ship's pods and hold, and what +N pods would add to each trip.
Renaming your ship (renameship) moves everything we knew about it (its info, readouts and limits) to the new name.
Typed: shiplimits (opens Ship Stats), shiplimits <ship or type>, shiplimits read <ship>, shiplimits list.

The left-hand lists of Datanet, Help & guides, Journal, Shops, Trade, Storage and Dossiers are real lists now: icons, counts on the right, the page you're on lit, folders (Help groups, Shops planets) open with an arrow, and they scroll with the mouse wheel and a slim scroll bar in your theme's colours.

Trade routes: a proper chart. Each route has a bar for its credits an hour, its numbers in columns, a fuel or permit mark when it needs one, and a Fly button that hands it to Auto Cargo. Hover a route for its legs (what to buy where).
Character > Gear & goals: real check boxes for the pieces you wear, your best-in-slot list and what you wear now side by side, all 24 slots on one screen.
Ships > Ship DB: hull types, a hull's ships, owners, places, last seen and Find results are tables you click (sort by name, last seen or owner).
Windows lay themselves out for their real size the moment they open (some drew at their old size first).

The 3D see-through ship hulls stay your own choice (Ships > Ship maps, or 'map3d hull on|off'): a map update from someone with them on no longer adds them to your map when yours are off, and turning them on fills them in even on a map that came without them.

New look for the toolbar menus and every Ships, Automation and Settings page: real icons instead of text symbols, cards, big status tiles, planet buttons, radio buttons for landing pads, on/off switches and check boxes instead of [x] and underlined words, and buttons with icons (Start, Pause, Stop...).
Less text: menu entries are just an icon and a name (hover one for what it does), and the long explanations on the pages are gone or tucked into the hover text.

Everything fits the window: long lists (your ships, sales, lanes, stats) turn pages with arrow buttons instead of running off the bottom or the right edge, and the text windows (Trade, Shops, Help, Datanet, Journal, Storage...) wrap their lines instead of cutting them off.
Windows open bigger, and remember where you put them: move or resize one and it opens that way next time (Settings > Theme > Reset window sizes puts them back).
Settings > Theme shows each theme as a card with its own corner art and colours: click one to use it.
The Map tab's 2D | 3D button moved to the top right: at the bottom left it sat on Mudlet's own map buttons.

Fix: a damaged save file (Mudlet closing in the middle of saving) can no longer stop any OmiLOTJ part from loading: the file is kept aside as <name>.broken-<date>, that part starts fresh, and it tells you once. Before, only the accent did this.

Fix: a second damaged accent file is kept too (it used to stay in place and warn at every load), an empty accent file now counts as damaged, and a hail reply says so when the accent couldn't be applied.
Fix: 'map3d hull' with no on/off (or a typo) no longer switches the hull on, and switching it to what it already is doesn't rebuild the map; the hull isn't added on a Mudlet without the 3D mapper.

3D map: every ship with a picture gets a see-through hull, glowing outlines of its shape between and around its decks, so it reads like a hologram of the ship with the rooms inside. 3D only: the 2D map stays exactly as it was. Switch it on Ships > Ship maps (or 'map3d hull off').

The Star Galleon, Vigo and JumpMaster pictures are redrawn to fit the rooms as they're really mapped (the Star Galleon's was far too small), and they now show under every deck of the ship, not just the entrance.
The Map tab's 2D | 3D button moved to the bottom left: at the top it covered the room name the 3D view writes there.

Fix: if your accent settings file got damaged (for example Mudlet closing in the middle of saving it), every say, sayto, whisper and so on showed a red 'Omi Accent ... attempt to index field data' error. Now the damaged file is kept aside as omi_accent.dat.broken, the accent starts fresh (off) and tells you once. A '!' line no longer goes out with the '!' when something goes wrong (the game read it as 'repeat my last command'), and a hail reply is never stopped by the accent.

New (Mudlet 5.1 or newer): the Map tab can show the map in 3D with Mudlet's new 3D mapper, to see ships with several decks from an angle. Ships > Ship maps has the buttons: 3D on/off, seven looks (Tiles, Blueprint, Terminal, Transit, Hologram, Ink wash, Diorama), views (Iso from a corner like old Diablo, Angled, Top, Side), turn, closer, further, darker other decks. Off puts the 2D map back with every setting as it was; the map itself is never changed. Optional: 3D by itself aboard a ship, 2D again when you leave. Typed: map3d.

The Map tab has a small 2D | 3D button in its top left corner that flips the map (move it to the top right or hide it on Ships > Ship maps). For both at once, 'pop-out map' opens a second map window that follows you around: click its own 3D button once.
Fix: the turbolift's old small white numbers showed through the new LED digits on the buttons and the floor readout. Now only the LED digits show.

Fix: the turbolift and the landing/docking panels show their intended colours: green directory lines, amber for where the lift is going, red for ACCESS DENIED and for pads that refused you (all of it showed white before).

New: GNI TradeCasts are tracked. A demand spike (sell that cargo there) or an oversupply (buy it there) brings up an alert saying where to buy or sell it from your price scans, with a link to check the price now. Trade routes that use the event are marked, and the routes page shows what's on. Trade > TradeCasts lists every event: how long they last, how far apart they come, how far the price moved and how long it took to recover, and roughly when the next one is due.

The turbolift panel's floor buttons and floor readout now show LED-clock seven-segment digits on dark glass, bigger and easier to read: amber, green where you are, bright where it's going, red when refused (the readout says 'no').

Fix: Settings > Action timers wouldn't open ('bad argument #3 to format'), the Landing Pads page broke on a pad with ships seen on it, and a dossier's ship never showed its 'open <ship>' link for a rename lead.

Action timer: new bars for turning (any course change, the maneuver you can do other things during), approach, first aid, disable security and the Tibanna harvester, with lengths measured from your own recordings.

Turning, launching and landing are learned per ship: your ship's own times first, then its hull type's, then a line over every ship you've flown and its Maneuver stat, so a ship you've never flown starts with a close estimate. The bar shows which ship (Settings > Action timers lists each ship's times).

New: a landing panel pops out (where the turbolift panel does) the moment you orbit a planet while flying by hand, with its landing pads as buttons. It marks your pick, your clan's pads and pads that refused you. Hidden pads that aren't in the game's list are learned when you land on one, and listed after that.

New: a docking panel shows when you dock with another ship, with buttons to undock now, in 10 seconds, cancel, or transfer fuel. When you're not docked, it lists the ships on your last radar to dock with (a saved docking code goes with the dock). Both panels switch on and off on Ships > Galaxy map.

New: Automation > Training, skill drills that need triggers and time. Slicer files runs encrypt_file then decrypt_file on yourself, round after round; Ponder ponders again each time it ends (it replaces the old always-on ponder trigger). Start, pause, resume and stop, with timer bars, waiting for Auto Cargo, Fly To and Ship DB lookups. Bot mode sends 'bot start' first so it's legal while you step away, shows the bot time left, pauses at the cooldown and can start again after it. Buttons for AutoStudy and autoresearch sit on the same page.
Action timer: encrypt and decrypt bars, and a fix: 'You stop what you were doing.' (a hyperjump or any command cutting a skill off) now stops the bar.

Jumping out is now timed from your ship's live position (GMCP, about once a second) and real speed, against everything on the radar including other ships, instead of a launch clock plus a safety margin. Auto Cargo and Fly To press hyper right at the edge. If another ship is in the way, one fresh radar shows where it is instead of a blind 20-second wait. The exact clear distance is learned from what the game says.

Flying by hand: a 'Clear to jump' bar while you fly out, a notice the moment you're clear, and an option to press hyper by itself then once the jump is calculated (Ships > Galaxy map > JUMPING, or 'getclear hyper on').
Galaxy tab: each hyperlane shows its length in parsecs in the middle of the line, for a quick read of how far a jump is.

New page Ships > Galaxy map: buttons for the lane distances (every lane / only lanes you've tried / off), untried lanes, the range ring and the planned route, plus every lane you know with its distance and where it was learned (forget a wrong one there).

Action timer fix: walking away from a ponder left its bar running. It now stops on 'Your thoughts turn from pondering...', and any skill you're busy with (the [*] in your prompt) stops its bar when the prompt goes back to [ ], so a study, dig or research cut short no longer leaves a bar behind.

Ship DB fix: looking out of a cockpit at a landing pad saved the view as a separate pad, with no planet or with the planet you'd been on before the flight (one Ryloth pad turned into 7 entries and 3 places). The view now counts as the pad itself, the ship you're sitting in is counted as being on it, and the copies already saved are merged once.

Ship DB keeps track of ships that may have been renamed or destroyed. A ship that stops having a record is marked missing. A new name of the same hull that turns up where it vanished becomes a rename lead, scored by pad, owner and timing, and a pad tells you on the spot. You confirm a rename, rule one out, or mark a ship destroyed (Ships > Ship DB > missing & renames). Your old lookups are read once, so ships that never had a record are skipped by 'Look up new'.

Ship DB lookups now say which ship they're on: '[shipdb] Locating MerrTrade01 (YT-1000 Light Freighter)  3 of 12', with retries marked, and a note when they wait for Auto Cargo or Fly To to reach hyperspace.
Ship DB fix: ships taking off ('Bejeweled [Launching]') were saved as extra ships, and a pad's '[Security]' tag made one pad count as two places. Both are merged.

Ship DB is now a database you can browse (Ships > Ship DB): every hull type, then every ship of that type, then one ship's file (where it's been seen, its owners over time, the dossiers that list it, its readouts). Click an owner to see everything they own and open their dossier; click a place to see every ship seen there. A Find box searches ships, owners and places. Dossiers and Landing Pads link back into it.

New: Journal > ITEMS, a record of every item that changes hands, with the time and the room. It covers what you give, slip, drop, pick up, put away, buy and sell, what's given to you, and what others give, drop or pick up around you. Your older logs are read once for it, so it goes back to your first session.
Journal search: a line repeated many times (a look spammed, an inventory listed) now shows once, with a count and when it was last seen, so it no longer pushes the older matches off the page.

New: the Galaxy tab shows your planned route in green while Fly To or Auto Cargo is flying (amber rings = refuel stops, green rings = where you trade or land at the end). Each lane goes back to its usual colour once you've flown it. Pausing keeps the route on the map; stopping or arriving clears it. Auto Cargo shows the rest of the loop, back to where the run started. 'lanes route off' hides it.

Auto Cargo no longer refuses a route with a leg longer than one tank. It plans refuel stops within your ship's range (Arkania > Tatooine in a YT-1000 = Arkania > Ryloth > Ithor > Tatooine), and at each one it lands, refuels and flies on without trading. A lane that turns out closed, or fuel running short, gets a new plan on the spot.

Trade routes count those refuel stops: each leg is timed the way Auto Cargo will fly it, so a route across the galaxy no longer looks like the best money. Route names show the stops, e.g. 'Arkania > (Ryloth: refuel) > (Ithor: refuel) > Tatooine'.

New: Fly To (Automation > Fly To, or type  flyto <planet>). Stand on the pad outside your ship and it flies you there: refuel, board, walk to the cockpit, launch, jump, land, walk out, close the ship, refuel.

Too far for one tank? It plans the quickest chain of refuel stops your ship's range allows, and flies around closed hyperlanes. A lane that turns out closed, or fuel running short, gets a new plan on the spot.

Pick your ship from YOUR SHIPS on the page (from 'ships owned' / 'ships clan'). The walk from the hatch to the cockpit comes from the hull's ship map; a hull never seen: walk it once yourself and type 'pilot', it's remembered.

Landing pads: pick one per planet (on the page, or it asks once you're in orbit). Your pick is kept and used every time, by Auto Cargo too, so the game's pad list isn't asked for on every landing any more.
The old community Autoflight's 'flyto' is switched off (its other commands still work).

New toolbar: the ten buttons are now six menus plus a gear. Character (Gear & goals, Storage), People (Journal, Dossiers), Money (Trade routes, Shops, Bank), Ships (Ship stats, Ship DB, Landing pads, Ship maps), Automation (Auto Cargo, Fly Loop, Ark Run), Library (Clan datanet, Help & guides), and the gear: Theme, Action timers, Updates. Click a menu, then a window; each entry says what it is. With a menu open, moving along the bar opens the next one; menus close when the mouse leaves.
A green dot on Automation while something runs (amber when paused), and its menu says which one.
A new look everywhere, like the Bank: rounded gradient buttons and frames in your class theme's colours (Settings > Theme), the same in every window.

Automation pages (Auto Cargo, Fly Loop, Ark Run) and Ship DB have real Start / Pause / Resume / Stop buttons above the page instead of text links. The Utilities button is gone: its pages are in the Ships, Automation and Settings menus.

Settings > Action timers: every bar, how long it takes (learned or a guess), bars on / off, a test bar, forget a time. Settings > Updates: your version, the map, auto-check on / off, what's new, Check now.

Ship numbers follow the ship you're in: boarding a ship makes it the current one, and its own 'info' (speed, hyperspeed, maneuver, fuel) is used, so two YT-1000s with different upgrades get different jump, range and hyper-wait figures. A ship you haven't 'info'd uses its type's stock numbers and says so once, with a click-to-read [info] link; a brand-new type borrows the numbers of another ship of that type you have 'info'd. (Fixed: the game's size class, like 'Modified Freighter', was being read as the ship type.)
New progress bars, found in your logs: studying (45 s), research (30 s), databank lookup (33 s), digging, securing, recharging a datapad, pondering.

Auto Cargo and Fly Loop no longer spam 'hyper' after a launch. A ship flies speed / 10 units a second and must be 500 units from everything, so they wait 500 / (speed / 10) seconds after leaving the pad, plus 2: YT-1000 ~73 s, Flashfire ~55 s, Star Commuter ~85 s (your logs agree to a second or two), then press hyper once. If another ship sits close (radar) or you turned onto a faster way out, they wait for that instead. If the game still says 'too close', they try again after the next position update (it used to try every 6 seconds). While the ship is still turning they wait for 'Maneuver complete.' instead of asking again and again.

New: smart taxis in every speedwalk ('sp', map clicks, walk-there links). Each hail teaches where its destination drops you, and whether the room you hailed from works (outside), says 'go outside' (inside) or gets no answer (the wilds). When a speedwalk would be clearly shorter by walking to a known hail spot, hailing and walking the rest, it does that and tells you. It only hails from rooms where a taxi has come before, so it never wanders around trying. Arkania, Lorrd and Wroona are known from the recordings. 'taxis' shows what's known, 'taxis off' turns it off ('taxi' is still the game's shuttle command).

Trade and Auto Cargo now fly around closed hyperlanes. A lane known to be blocked (red on the Galaxy map: Ryloth - Lorrd and Arkania - Lorrd right now) is never suggested straight any more: the route goes via a system in between (Eeropha) and its distance, time and credits per hour count the longer way and the extra jump. A route with no way through at all isn't suggested. Auto Cargo makes the stop itself (jump to Eeropha, calculate again, jump on to the planet), and if a lane turns out to be blocked mid-run it notes it and takes the way around instead of stopping.

Each stop on a way around now says what it is: 'just passing through' when your fuel lasts to the end (you only drop out, calculate and jump on), or 'LAND and refuel at ...' when it won't (Eeropha's Refueling Outpost, or the planets in that system). You see it under the leg in Trade, in 'flight <planet>', and from Auto Cargo when it plans the jump. At a refuel stop Auto Cargo pauses with the reminder; land, refuel, launch, then 'autocargo resume' gets clear and jumps on. A refuel stop also counts in the route's time per loop.

Bank: a new look. Every account is its own row with real buttons (Deposit, Withdraw, Balance, From / To, Close; Close asks 'SURE?' first), the totals sit at the top (in the bank, on hand, at a bank), and quick amounts (10k, 100k, 1M, all cash on hand) fill the Amount box. History and known banks moved to their own tabs, so a deposit no longer pushes your accounts down the page.

Landing (Auto Cargo): any pad will do now, garages included (cargo trades there too), picked at random. Your own clan's pads come first (the safest; your clan is read from 'score'), other clans' pads only as a last resort. A pad that answers "Restricted Landing pad" is skipped for that character from then on, whoever sent the land. A planet whose pads aren't known yet gets a plain 'land <planet>' first to list them. 'pads <planet>' shows CLAN / ok / other / refused per pad.

New: Smart Exits. Doors you open with a command now work by walking: on Arkania's Mountainside Road just type 'se' and it pushes the palm for the city airlock; at Merr-Sonn's secured doors the direction says 'enter' / 'exit' for you. 15 doors from the recordings are built in (Arkania, Merr-Sonn, Kala'uun spaceport, Lorrd spaceport, Kafrene). A new door learns itself: open it once with say / push / press and walk through, and from then on the direction does it. Speedwalks and map clicks use them too. 'sx' lists a room's, 'sx se push palm' adds one, 'sx se remove' takes one out.

Fixed: the hyperlane lines and jump-range ring didn't show on the Galaxy tab (they were drawn behind the starfield). The untested grey lanes are brighter too, and lanes learned while another tab is open appear when you open the Galaxy tab.
Fixed: 'flight', the range ring and Ship Stats now know your ship after a restart while you're aboard (from the room you're in, and the last ship you boarded).

Ship Stats: type any number of units to add in the new box (1, 50, 1000...), or click +1 / +5 / +10 / +50 / +100 / +1000. Every row now counts real units (no more x10 / x100), and shows how many more of each fit in the ship's free quota.

New: Omi Flight. 'flight' shows your ship's real numbers, worked out from 83 recorded flights: a jump takes 500 x parsecs / hyperspeed seconds, fuel = the ship's fuel-per-parsec x parsecs (YT-1000 229, Flashfire 80), realspace speed / 10 units a second, and every Maneuver point under 100 adds half a second to launches, landings and turns. 'flight <planet>' = a jump from where you are: time, fuel, the whole leg. Help > Guides > Flight.

Getting clear to jump: after every launch the radar is read and, if another ship sits in your way, a course is set the fastest way to 500 units from everything. 'getclear' does it by hand (it speeds back up first if you were stopped).

TRACTOR BEAM alarm: the moment a ship locks on, Auto Cargo and the Fly Loop pause and STAY paused (a checkpoint, a pirate or an enemy: you decide). When it's sorted, 'autocargo resume' speeds back up and either gets clear and jumps again, or flies on to land.

New: hyperlanes on the Galaxy tab. White lines = lanes that work (a calculation went through, a jump was made, or the hyperlane monitor says Passable), red = blocked (interference, or No Route on the monitor), grey dashes = never tried but within your ship's range. A ring around you shows how far you can jump with the fuel aboard (fainter: a full tank). 'l monitor' with a handheld hyperlane status monitor (Lodestar station, Eeropha) fills them in. 'lanes' lists them.

New: Utilities > Ship Stats. Every ship stat with what one point (or +5, +10, +20) is worth: seconds off a jump, faster in and out, range, hull, weapons fire rate, plus the quota and credit cost. Works for any ship you've done 'info' on, so you can show customers what an upgrade buys them.

Fixed: 'radar' was sent twice after every launch and every jump (Autoflight sent one even when it wasn't flying). Blocked hyperspace routes ('interference') are remembered and flagged in Trade. Ship DB lookups now wait for the quiet minutes in hyperspace during Auto Cargo, instead of sending the dockworkers away.

New: Auto Cargo. In Trade, click 'auto cargo' on any route, choose the planet you start on and your cargo ship (Utilities > Auto Cargo), stand on that pad outside the ship and press START. Each stop it checks the hold (listcargo), sells what it brought, buys the next cargo (fewer units if you can't afford a full hold), boards, closes the hatch, walks to the cockpit, flies, lands, walks out, closes the hatch behind you and refuels to full. Watch the screen while it runs (HELP BOTTING). Help > Guides > Auto Cargo.

Ships you have clan or owner rights to just open; a ship someone lent you opens with its hatch code (type it once in the code box). The walk to the cockpit is built in per ship class (YT-1000, Flashfire); others can be added with 'autocargo class'.
Trade: 'Scan all planets' now asks every planet at once instead of one every 5 seconds (any that fail are asked again once).

Trade: profits are now after the selling planet's tax, permits you buy are remembered (the route stops saying 'permit'), and the credits-per-hour figures switch to real timings as soon as Auto Cargo has flown a leg.

New: Action timer. In the bottom-right corner of the main window a bar fills up while something takes time (two at once stack, each with its name and time above it): loading or unloading cargo, launching, jump calculations, hyperspace (it follows the game's countdown), landing, turbolifts, locateship. It learns how long each one really takes (amber = still a guess, green = learned). 'atimer' lists them, 'atimer off' hides it.

Landing: Auto Cargo picks a pad at random among a planet's allowed ones each time (Arkania: Alpha or Beta, Bespin: Platform 327 or 401, Naboo: Theed only), never a garage or a clan pad, and tries the next if one refuses. New planets: their first pad, then the next. Set your own: 'pads use <planet> = <pad>, <pad>', 'pads avoid <planet> = <pad>'.
Toolbar panels (Datapad, Help, Trade, Utilities...) now open and close instantly instead of sliding in: snappier, and no more half-finished slides.

Turbolifts: the Cloud City lifts on Bespin work now (their directory has a blank line that cut the reading short; floors 221, 317, 327 and 401 are built in), and a bug that saved nonsense floor rooms is fixed.

New: Turbolift panel. Inside a turbolift an elevator panel slides in beside the map and chat: the lift's directory on a screen and round floor buttons. Click one to ride there. It already knows the Merr-Sonn, Ryloth City, East Hangar and Academy lifts; any other lift is learned the first time you look at its panel, plate or directory. Help > Guides > Turbolifts.

The panel shows your CURRENT FLOOR like a real lift: learned when the doors open after a ride, and from the room you walk in from (each room beside a lift belongs to a floor; it learns more every time you step out).

Ship maps: the YT-1000 picture is bigger and lined up with its rooms (the cockpit corridor and cockpit were floating above the ship), and its cockpit, one floor up, has its own picture: go up and the map shows the cockpit pod instead of an empty background. Pictures now update themselves on your map when a new version changes them.

Ships: 'stat' aboard a ship is now kept too (hull, shields, fuel, ammo, cargo), next to its 'info'. Both show on the ship's Storage page and in 'shipdb <ship>' (access codes hidden until you click show codes).
Accent: a grumble like ", eh" now only comes at the end of a sentence, never in the middle of one ("a betta deal, eh dan dat" was the old way). An "eh" you type yourself is always kept.
Fixed: the accent now works on 'clan <text>' (the short way to type clantalk), not just 'clantalk'.
Fixed: an accent phrase's result is no longer changed again word by word (a phrase that gave "no have" could come out as "nah have").
Accent: 'accent list' shows every word and phrase your accent uses (your style's and your own), and how often the sometimes-changes happen.

Accent now starts blank for everyone: build your character's own voice with 'accent swap <word> = <new>' and 'accent phrase <words> = <new>', try it with 'accent test <text>', then 'accent on'. (The Toydarian voice from 1.13.0 was the owner's own and isn't included any more.) Help > Guides > Accent.

Accent: 'accent review' lists the sentences that went out exactly as you typed them, so missing words are easy to spot. What you say is kept as typed and as sent in your own omi_accent_log.txt (never shared).

New: Accent. Your character's way of talking goes on what you say in character (say, sayto, whisper, CommNet, clan, broadcast, hails, quoted speech in emotes). Built in: a Watto-like Toydarian voice ('That sounds exciting' -> 'Dat sounds excitin''). Off until you type 'accent on'; 'accent test <text>' shows it first, '!' before a line sends it as typed. Help > Guides > Accent.

Ship DB: back at a pad you've seen before, it lists every ship that arrived since your last visit: NEW if you've never seen it anywhere, otherwise its owner (and their clan) and where it was last seen, with a [locate] link to look it up straight away. The first visit to a pad is still just one line.

Ark Run: lommite now digs 10 rooms along the tunnel through Mount Ravkin (it was 2). With lommite switched on, the run walks the whole tunnel from the west end out to the Mining Village Entrance, digging as it goes: only 6 more commands than the normal loop. Still off by default (Utilities > Ark Run).

Fixed: a 'dub' or 'greet' that fails ("They aren't here.") is no longer saved in your memory log, however often you retry it. Lines that just happened to arrive meanwhile (like an interrupted study) are left out of memory records too.

Journal: CommNet channels have names. General (0), Confederacy (1), Republic (1024), Durafly (455) and Merr-Sonn (5555) each get their own entry under Recordings; frequencies without a name sit under 'Other frequencies'.
Name any channel as you learn whose it is: 'name this channel' on its page, or 'journal freq <number> = <name>'. Your names stay on your computer.
People pages and dossiers say where someone was heard: 'General 12, Republic 3, clan comms 5, in person 2'.
Fixed: a 'locateship' you type yourself is now kept too (before, only 'shipdb locate' runs were), so the owner's dossier gets the ship.
Dossiers: anyone who talks on your clan comms gets their clan, division and rank filled in (only members can talk there). Your old clan-comm recordings are read once too.

Dossiers: clan members you only know by a description ('A Human male') are listed on the Dossiers home page under UNNAMED, with their race, rank and last lines. Click 'name them' once you know who it is.
Fixed: a dossier showed only the name and nothing else (one of its links was missing the hover text Mudlet requires). Every panel's links now always have one.
Fixed: 'lookup' now reads any databank file, however the player laid it out (NAME: / SPECIES: / ALLEGIANCE: style too), and keeps the whole file in the dossier.
Guides: Help (toolbar) now starts with OMILOTJ GUIDES, a short how-to page for every tool we've built. Type 'guide' to open them, or 'guide <word>' (guide dossiers, guide arkrun, guide shipdb...).

Dossiers fill themselves in with what the game tells you outright: someone introducing themself (or you to them), a dub, 'lookup' with a datapad (race, sex, level, clan and rank, and the whole databank file), 'locateship' owners (the ship goes into their file), 'memory' (names and how they look), and every name the Journal knows. Each file gets a contact log of when and where you met.

Ship DB notes ships in space too: the ones you see out of the cockpit while flying (the bright yellow list) and every ship on 'radar', with the system and the planet they were near. New ones join the list for 'shipdb locate'.
The chat wrap fix from 1.8.1 really is in this one (the 1.8.1 download went out without it).

Fixed: chat tabs could wrap lines far too short (a few words per line in a wide box) when the chat's width was measured while Mudlet was still opening. The wrap now follows the chat box's real width (new lines; older lines keep their wrapping).

Dossiers (new toolbar button): your own file on each person, like a records database. Clan, rank, profession, who they work for, race, base, plus lists of other names, disguises you've seen, restrung armor looks, ships, shops and notes. You fill it in as you work things out; nothing fills itself in.
Every entry remembers when you wrote it and where you were, and is tagged IC (learned in play), PUB (public) or OOC (don't use it in character). Changing someone's clan keeps the old one as history.

Clues next to what you wrote: where the Ship DB saw each of their ships (which pads), the shop catalog's stock, and what your recordings hold (lines by or about them, also under each disguise, memory notes, thoughts).

Ship DB lookups work now: it reads the real locateship answer (owner, dock, planet), waits for each lookup to finish before starting the next (sending the next one early cut every lookup off), and tries again after 'no record found' or an interruption. Ships whose earlier lookups got nothing are looked up again by 'shipdb locate'.

Search finds people by any ship, disguise, name or note. 'dossier <name> ship = <ship>' adds things from the command line; Journal person pages get an 'open dossier' link. Dossiers stay on your PC: they're never shared.
Fixed: the Utilities button didn't open on screens where the toolbar is narrow (the version number sat on top of it). The buttons now shrink to fit.
Fixed: a long hail could get the next game message stuck onto its end in the hail window (like 'You are too close to ... to make the jump to lightspeed!').
Fixed: toolbar buttons often needed two or three clicks. A click while a panel is still sliding now waits its turn instead of being ignored, and the button lights up the moment you click it.

Ark Run: choose what to gather (crate, wireless, test results, crystal chips, frozen organisms, the tunnel credit, Arkanian diamonds, blue diamonds, lommite) in Utilities > Ark Run or with 'arkrun gather <kind> on|off'. Start takes the shortest loop for what's switched on.
Ark Run: type your locker number in the box on the Ark Run page (or 'arkrun locker <n>'). Each player sets their own; too-heavy pickups go there and the pickaxe comes from it.
Not gathering crates: the run goes straight away and, after the loop, waits for the city's reset line before going again.
Ship maps mark the rooms that matter: cockpits yellow 'C', turrets red 'T', engine rooms green 'E' (rooms the game tags [ENGINE], or with Engine in the name).
Every ship already on your map gets marked when Mudlet starts, and every ship of a class shares the marks.
Clan private datanet: 'dncrawl MS private' (any clan you belong to) also saves the members-only pages, kept apart in their own folder and marked with the character who read them.
Datapad: members-only pages show in orange under their clan, in a MEMBERS ONLY section below the public pages.
Ark Run: no more lommite digging in the tunnel (the blue diamond digs stay), and after emptying your pockets into the locker it takes your comlinks back out, so you can still hear and talk.
Ship pictures: the Naboo N-1 Starfighter now has one under its map, and the LAAT/s Gunship's picture shows up (its name was wrong).

Ship DB: every ship you pass (pads, hangars, the view from your cockpit) is noted quietly with where it was seen. 'shipdb locate' (or Utilities > Ship DB) runs locateship on the new ones, from anywhere; owners are kept as a history, so a sold ship shows who had it before. 'shipdb owner <name>' lists what someone owns.
Fixed: in space the ship bar flickered over the bottom of the game text (and its scrollbar) about once a second.

Themes: framed map, chat, bottom and ship bars plus matching toolbar colours, one look per class (combat, piloting, engineering, bounty hunting, smuggling, leadership, espionage, slicer, medical, science, force) or the plain datapad look.
The theme follows your main class (the cyan one in 'score' or 'levels'); pick any other with 'theme <name>' or Utilities > Themes. The ship bar's frame only shows while you're in a ship.
Click the version number on the toolbar: what's new, and an instant check for updates.
Ship pictures on the map: a top-down drawing of the ship sits under its map, lined up with the rooms (you see the Flashfire with you in its cockpit).
Drawn so far: Flashfire, Star Commuter shuttle, JumpMaster 5000, YT-1000, Star Galleon, LAAT/s, Vigo gunship. 'shipmap art nudge <east> <north>' fine-tunes the spot.
Aboard a ship the map zooms in so the ship fills it, and zooms back out when you leave ('shipmap zoom off' to stop it, 'shipmap zoom <n>' for n rooms across).
Recordings skip the whole login screen (account, passwords, character list): they start right after your last password, at the Message of the Day or 'Reconnecting'.
Recording (rec) starts by itself every time Mudlet starts; 'rec off' stops it until the next start. Your login is never recorded.
Update check the moment you log in (your first room in the game), then every 15 minutes from there.
Update window: the buttons show each step (Downloading... / Installing... / Updated), extra clicks are ignored while it works, and it closes by itself when done.
Buttons with nothing to do are greyed out instead of disappearing; the map asks for a second click before it replaces yours.
Updates are also checked when you connect and every 15 minutes, not only when Mudlet starts. 'Later' means no reminder for that version until you restart Mudlet.
Ship map areas are named after the ship's class ('Star Commuter 2000 Transport'), not each ship: one area per class, all its ships share it.
Old per-ship areas (PUB04, PUB10, PUB29, your own ships) are folded into their class areas by themselves when Mudlet loads.
A class's blueprint is learned from the map as soon as you board one, even right after Mudlet starts.
Ship maps: one blueprint per ship class. Board any ship of a mapped class (every Star Commuter shuttle, every Flashfire) and its whole map is drawn at once.
Map a new class once (board, 'map start', walk it, leave) and it works in every ship of that class. Blueprints come with updates.
Utilities > Ship Maps lists the blueprints; 'shipmap' does the same in the main window.
Version numbers: shown on the toolbar (click for this list).
Updates from inside Mudlet: new versions and maps are offered in a pop-up when the profile loads ('omiupdate' checks now). This is the last package you install by hand.
Utilities button: Fly Loop (your own ship, any two planets, landing pads), Landing Pads list, Ark Run controls.
Hail pop-up: ship hails open a movable window in the middle of the screen; reply from it. 'hails' opens it.
Bank: 'bank list' now works with any prompt (it waited for one particular prompt before).
Landing pads are learned whenever you type 'land <planet>' in orbit without a pad ('pads' lists them).
